title.zh: 卷五十一 雜傳第三十九: 朱守殷 董璋 范延光 婁繼英 安重榮 安從進 楊光遠
title.en: Volume 51 Miscellaneous Biographies 31: Zhu Shouyin, Dong Zhang, Fan Yanguang, Lou Jiying, An Zhongrong, An Congjin, Yang Guangyuan
title.raw: 卷五十一 雜傳第三十九: 朱守殷 董璋 范延光 婁繼英 安重榮 安從進 楊光遠 Volume 51 Miscellaneous Biographies 31: Zhu Shouyin, Dong Zhang, Fan Yanguang, Lou Jiying, An Zhongrong, An Congjin, Yang Guangyuan

sentences.zh: 朱守殷

translations.literal: Zhu Shouyin
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin

sentences.zh: 朱守殷，少事唐莊宗為奴，名曰會兒。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouyin, in youth served Tang's Zhuangzong as a slave; his name was Hui'er.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin had served Tang Zhuangzong as a slave in his youth; his name was Hui'er.

sentences.zh: 莊宗讀書，會兒常侍左右。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong studied, Hui'er constantly attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong read his books, Hui'er was always at his side.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，以其廝養為長直軍，以守殷為軍使，故未嘗經戰陣之用。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he made his household attendants the Changzhi Army and appointed Shouyin its commander; thus he had never been tested in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhuangzong took the throne, he formed his personal attendants into the Changzhi Army and made Shouyin its commander, so he had never seen real combat.

sentences.zh: 然好言人陰私長短以自結，莊宗以為忠，遷蕃漢馬步軍都虞候，使守德勝。

translations.literal: Yet he loved to speak of others' private faults and merits to win favor; Zhuangzong thought him loyal and promoted him to chief adjutant of the Fan-Han horse and foot armies, posting him at Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in retailing others' secrets to curry favor. Zhuangzong took this for loyalty, made him chief adjutant of the combined horse and foot forces, and stationed him at Desheng.

sentences.zh: 王彥章攻德勝，守殷無備，遂破南城，莊宗罵曰：「駑才，果誤予事！

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang attacked Desheng; Shouyin was unprepared and the southern citadel was taken. Zhuangzong cursed him: "Worthless fool—you have indeed ruined my affair!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang attacked Desheng. Shouyin was caught off guard and lost the southern citadel. Zhuangzong raged: "You worthless fool—you have ruined me!

sentences.zh: 」明宗請以守殷行軍法，莊宗不聽。

translations.literal: " Mingzong asked that Shouyin be punished under military law; Zhuangzong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong urged that Shouyin be executed under military law, but Zhuangzong refused.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，領鎮武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang he held the post of military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 2 he was made military governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 是時，莊宗初入洛，守殷巡檢校京師，恃恩驕恣，淩侮勛舊，與伶人景進相為表裏。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong had just entered Luoyang; Shouyin inspected and patrolled the capital, trusting in favor he grew arrogant, insulted meritorious veterans, and worked inside and out with the actor Jing Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had just entered Luoyang. Shouyin patrolled the capital, swaggering on imperial favor, bullying the old guard, and conspiring openly with the actor Jing Jin.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌已殺郭崇韜，進誣朱友謙與崇韜謀反，莊宗遣守殷圍其第而殺之。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji had already killed Guo Chongtao; Jin slandered Zhu Youqian as plotting rebellion with Chongtao, and Zhuangzong sent Shouyin to surround his residence and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei, Jiji, had already killed Guo Chongtao. Jing Jin accused Zhu Youqian of plotting with Chongtao, and Zhuangzong sent Shouyin to surround his mansion and kill him.

sentences.zh: 是時，明宗自鎮州來朝，居於私第。

translations.literal: At that time Mingzong came from Zhen prefecture to court and lodged in his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had come from Zhenzhou to court and was staying in his private house.

sentences.zh: 莊宗方惑群小，疑忌大臣，遣守殷伺察明宗動靜。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was then misled by petty men and suspicious of great ministers; he sent Shouyin to spy on Mingzong's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was listening to flatterers and had grown wary of his senior ministers. He sent Shouyin to watch Mingzong's every move.

sentences.zh: 守殷陰使人告明宗曰：「位高人臣者身危，功蓋天下者不賞，公可謂位高而功著矣。

translations.literal: Shouyin secretly sent someone to tell Mingzong: "When one stands high among ministers his person is in danger; when merit covers the realm he goes unrewarded—you may be called high in rank and eminent in merit.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyin secretly warned Mingzong: "A minister who stands too high risks his life; a man whose merit covers the realm goes unrewarded. You are high in rank and your deeds are plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 宜自圖歸藩，無與禍會也！

translations.literal: You should plan to return to your fief and not share in disaster!
translations.idiomatic: You ought to plan your return to your fief before disaster finds you!

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「吾洛陽一匹夫爾，何能為也！

translations.literal: " Mingzong said: "I am but a commoner of Luoyang—what could I do!
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong replied: "I am nobody in Luoyang—what could I possibly do?

sentences.zh: 」既而明宗卒反於魏。

translations.literal: " Before long Mingzong did rebel at Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward Mingzong rose in rebellion at Wei.

sentences.zh: 莊宗東討，守殷將騎軍陣宣仁門外以俟駕。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong campaigned east; Shouyin led the cavalry and arrayed them outside Xuaren Gate to await the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong marched east against him. Shouyin drew up the cavalry outside Xuaren Gate to await the emperor's departure.

sentences.zh: 郭從謙作亂，犯興教門以入，莊宗亟召守殷等軍，守殷按軍不動。

translations.literal: Guo Congqian mutinied, breached Xingjiao Gate to enter; Zhuangzong urgently summoned Shouyin's army, but Shouyin held his troops motionless.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congqian mutinied and broke in through Xingjiao Gate. Zhuangzong urgently summoned Shouyin's troops, but Shouyin held his men still.

sentences.zh: 莊宗獨與諸王宦官百餘人射賊，守殷等終不至，方移兵憩北邙山下，聞莊宗已崩，即馳入宮中，選載嬪御、寶貨以歸，縱軍士劫掠，遣人趣明宗入洛。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong alone with princes, eunuchs, and a hundred-odd others shot at the rebels; Shouyin and the rest never came. Only then did he move the army to rest on Mount Beimang; hearing Zhuangzong had fallen, he galloped into the palace, chose concubines and treasure to carry home, let soldiers plunder, and sent men to hurry Mingzong into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong fought the rebels with barely a hundred princes and eunuchs at his side. Shouyin never came. Only then did he move his army to rest on Mount Beimang. When he heard Zhuangzong was dead, he galloped into the palace, loaded concubines and treasure onto his carts, let his men loot the city, and sent word urging Mingzong to enter Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 守殷之將反也，召都指揮使馬彥超與計事，彥超不從，守殷殺之。

translations.literal: As Shouyin was about to rebel he summoned chief commander Ma Yanchao to plan with him; Yanchao refused and Shouyin killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouyin was plotting rebellion he summoned chief commander Ma Yanchao to counsel with him. Yanchao refused, and Shouyin killed him.

sentences.zh: 明宗憐彥超之死，以其子承祚為洺州長史。

translations.literal: Mingzong pitied Yanchao's death and appointed his son Chengduo chief magistrate of Luo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong pitied Yanchao's death and appointed his son Chengduo chief magistrate of Luo.

sentences.zh: ○董璋

translations.literal: ○ Dong Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang

sentences.zh: 董璋，不知其世家何人也。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang—his family origins are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang's family background is unknown.

sentences.zh: 少與高季興、孔循俱為汴州富人李讓家僮。

translations.literal: In youth he was, together with Gao Jixing and Kong Xun, a household slave of the Bianzhou magnate Li Rang.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had been a household slave of Li Rang, a wealthy man of Bianzhou, together with Gao Jixing and Kong Xun.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖鎮宣武，養讓為子，是為朱友讓。

translations.literal: Liang's Taizu held Xuanyi and adopted Rang as a son—this was Zhu Yourang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Taizu held Xuanyi, he adopted Rang as his son, who became Zhu Yourang.

sentences.zh: 其僮奴以友讓故，皆得事梁太祖，璋以軍功為指揮使。

translations.literal: Their slave attendants, because of Yourang, all came to serve Liang's Taizu; Zhang, through military merit, became a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Through Yourang's connection, the slaves all entered Taizu's service. Zhang rose to command through military merit.

sentences.zh: 晉李繼韜以潞州叛降梁，末帝遣璋攻下澤州，即以璋為刺史。

translations.literal: Jin's Li Jitao rebelled with Lu prefecture and surrendered to Liang; the Last Emperor sent Zhang to capture Ze prefecture and at once made him its prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's Li Jitao rebelled and surrendered Lu to Liang, the Last Emperor sent Zhang to take Ze and made him its prefect.

sentences.zh: 梁亡，璋事唐為邠寧節度使，與郭崇韜相善。

translations.literal: When Liang fell, Zhang served Tang as military governor of Binning and was on good terms with Guo Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang fell, Zhang served Tang as military governor of Binning and was close to Guo Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 崇韜伐蜀，以璋為行營右廂馬步軍都虞候，軍事大小，皆與參決。

translations.literal: Chongtao campaigned against Shu and made Zhang chief adjutant of the right wing horse and foot of the field army; in military affairs great and small he joined in every decision.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao invaded Shu, he made Zhang chief adjutant of the right wing and consulted him on every matter, large or small.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，以為劍南東川節度使，孟知祥鎮西川。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was made military governor of Jiannan East Circuit; Meng Zhixiang held West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, he was made military governor of eastern Sichuan while Meng Zhixiang held the west.

sentences.zh: 其後，二人有異志。

translations.literal: Afterward the two men harbored separate ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward both men began to harbor ambitions of their own.

sentences.zh: 安重誨居中用事，議者多言知祥必不為唐用，而能制知祥者璋也，往往稱璋忠義，重誨以為然，頗優寵之，以故璋益橫。

translations.literal: An Chonghui held power at court; many in council said Zhixiang would surely not serve Tang, and that the one who could control Zhixiang was Zhang. They often praised Zhang's loyalty and righteousness; Chonghui believed it and favored him generously, so Zhang grew all the more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui dominated the court. Councillors said Zhixiang would never remain loyal to Tang and that only Zhang could restrain him. They praised Zhang's loyalty, Chonghui believed them, and showered him with favor—so Zhang grew ever more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 初，璋等反，唐獨誅璋家屬，知祥妻子皆在成都，其疏屬留京師者皆不誅。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhang and the others rebelled, Tang executed only Zhang's family; Zhixiang's wife and children were all in Chengdu, and his more distant kin left in the capital were not punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang and the others first rebelled, Tang executed only Zhang's family. Zhixiang's wife and children were in Chengdu, and his distant kin in the capital went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭討璋等，兵久無功，而自關以西饋運不給，遠近勞敝，明宗患之。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang campaigned against Zhang and the rest; the army long achieved nothing, and from Pass westward supplies failed—near and far were worn out, and Mingzong was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang campaigned against them without success. West of the passes supplies ran dry and the realm groaned under the burden. Mingzong was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 安重誨自往督軍，敬瑭不納，重誨遂得罪死，敬瑭亦還。

translations.literal: An Chonghui went in person to oversee the army; Jingtang would not receive him. Chonghui then fell from favor and died; Jingtang also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui went to supervise the army in person, but Jingtang refused him entry. Chonghui fell from power and died, and Jingtang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明宗乃遣西川進奏官蘇願、東川軍將劉澄西歸，諭璋等使改過。

translations.literal: Mingzong then sent the West Circuit memorial officer Su Yuan and the East Circuit general Liu Chengxi back west to instruct Zhang and the others to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent Su Yuan, memorial officer of western Sichuan, and Liu Chengxi, a general of the east, west to urge Zhang and the others to repent.

sentences.zh: 知祥遣人告璋，欲與俱謝過自歸，璋曰：「唐不殺孟公家族，於西川恩厚矣。

translations.literal: Zhixiang sent someone to tell Zhang he wished to submit together in acknowledgment of fault; Zhang said: "Tang did not kill Lord Meng's family—toward West Circuit the grace was thick.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang sent word that they should submit together and beg forgiveness. Zhang replied: "Tang spared Lord Meng's family—that was grace enough to western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 我子孫何在？

translations.literal: Where are my sons and grandsons?
translations.idiomatic: Where are my sons and grandsons?

sentences.zh: 何謝之有！

translations.literal: What is there to thank for!
translations.idiomatic: What is there to thank them for?

sentences.zh: 」璋由此疑知祥賣己。

translations.literal: " From this Zhang suspected Zhixiang had sold him out.
translations.idiomatic: " From that moment Zhang suspected Zhixiang had betrayed him.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，以兵萬人攻知祥，戰於彌牟，璋大敗，還走梓州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he attacked Zhixiang with ten thousand troops; they fought at Mimu; Zhang was greatly defeated and fled back to Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he attacked Zhixiang with ten thousand men. They fought at Mimu. Zhang was routed and fled to Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，唐陵州刺史王暉代還過璋，璋邀留之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tang's Ling prefect Wang Hui, returning on relief of office, passed Zhang's territory; Zhang detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Tang's prefect of Ling, Wang Hui, was returning home on relief of office, Zhang had detained him.

sentences.zh: 至是，暉執璋殺之，傳其首於知祥。

translations.literal: At this time Hui seized Zhang and killed him, sending his head to Zhixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Now Hui seized Zhang, killed him, and sent his head to Zhixiang.

sentences.zh: 範延光

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang

sentences.zh: 範延光，字子瑰，相州臨漳人也。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang, style Zikui, was a man of Linzhang in Xiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang, courtesy name Zikui, was from Linzhang in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗為節度使，置延光麾下，而未之奇也。

translations.literal: When Tang's Mingzong was military governor he placed Yanguang under his command but did not regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was a military governor he placed Yanguang in his command but saw nothing remarkable in him.

sentences.zh: 明宗破鄆州，梁兵方扼楊劉，其先鋒將康延孝陰送款於明宗。

translations.literal: Mingzong took Yan prefecture; Liang's troops were then blocking Yangliu, and their vanguard general Kang Yanxiao secretly sent overtures of surrender to Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took Yanzhou, Liang's army was holding Yangliu. Their vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao secretly offered to defect to Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 明宗求可以通延孝款於莊宗者，延光輒自請行，乃懷延孝蠟丸書，西見莊宗致之，且曰：「今延孝雖有降意，而梁兵扼楊劉者甚盛，未可圖也，不如築壘馬家口以通汶陽。

translations.literal: Mingzong sought someone who could convey Yanxiao's overture to Zhuangzong; Yanguang at once volunteered to go. He bore Yanxiao's wax-sealed letter, went west to see Zhuangzong and delivered it, and said: "Now though Yanxiao has intent to surrender, Liang's troops blocking Yangliu are very strong and cannot yet be attacked; better to build a fort at Majiakou to open Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong needed someone to carry Yanxiao's offer to Zhuangzong. Yanguang volunteered, bore the wax-sealed letter west, and told Zhuangzong: "Yanxiao wishes to surrender, but Liang's grip on Yangliu is too strong to attack yet. Build a fort at Majiakou to open the route to Wenyang instead.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗以為然。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 壘成，梁遣王彥章急攻新壘。

translations.literal: When the fort was finished, Liang sent Wang Yanzhang to press the attack on the new fort.
translations.idiomatic: When the fort was finished, Liang sent Wang Yanzhang to storm it.

sentences.zh: 明宗使延光間行求兵，夜至河上，為梁兵所得，送京師，下延光獄，搒掠數百，脅以白刃，延光終不肯言晉事。

translations.literal: Mingzong sent Yanguang by secret route to seek troops; by night he reached the river and was taken by Liang's soldiers, sent to the capital, and cast into prison. He was flogged hundreds of times and threatened with bare blades, yet Yanguang would not speak of Jin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent Yanguang by a secret route to seek reinforcements. He reached the river by night and was captured. Liang sent him to the capital, threw him in prison, flogged him hundreds of times, and held blades to his throat—but he would not betray Jin.

sentences.zh: 系之數月，稍為獄吏所獲。

translations.literal: He was confined for several months and was gradually won over by the prison clerks.
translations.idiomatic: After months in chains, the jailers gradually won him over.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，獄吏去其桎梏，拜而出之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, the prison clerks removed his fetters, bowed, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, the jailers removed his fetters, bowed, and set him free.

sentences.zh: 莊宗見延光，喜，拜檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong saw Yanguang, rejoiced, and appointed him honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong received him with delight and appointed him honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，為宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he was commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he served as commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明宗行幸汴州，至滎陽，朱守殷反，延光曰：「守殷反跡始見，若緩之使得為計，則城堅而難近。

translations.literal: Mingzong traveled to Bian prefecture; reaching Xingyang, Zhu Shouyin rebelled. Yanguang said: "Shouyin's rebellion has only just appeared; if we delay and let him make his plans, the walls will be strong and hard to approach.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong traveled to Bianzhou and reached Xingyang, Zhu Shouyin rebelled. Yanguang said: "His revolt has only just begun. If we give him time to prepare, the walls will harden and we will never get near.

sentences.zh: 故乘人之未備者，莫若急攻，臣請騎兵五百，馳至城下，以神速駭之。

translations.literal: Thus to strike before the enemy is prepared, nothing surpasses a swift attack. I ask for five hundred cavalry to gallop to the walls and dismay them with sudden speed.
translations.idiomatic: Strike before he is ready—nothing beats a sudden assault. Give me five hundred cavalry and I will ride to the walls and shock him with speed.

sentences.zh: 」乃以騎兵五百，自暮疾馳至半夜，行二百里，戰於城下。

translations.literal: " He took five hundred cavalry; from dusk they galloped hard until midnight, covering two hundred li, and fought below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: " He took five hundred horsemen, rode hard from dusk until midnight—two hundred li—and fought beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 遲明，明宗亦馳至，汴兵望見天子乘輿，乃開門，而延光先入，猶巷戰，殺傷甚眾，守殷死，汴州平。

translations.literal: At dawn Mingzong also galloped up; Bian's troops, seeing the Son of Heaven's carriage, opened the gates. Yanguang entered first; fighting still raged in the lanes and casualties were heavy. Shouyin died and Bian prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Mingzong arrived. The defenders saw the imperial carriage and opened the gates. Yanguang entered first; street fighting left many dead. Shouyin was killed and Bianzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷樞密使，出為成德軍節度使。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Privy Commissioner and sent out as military governor of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Privy Commissioner, then was posted out as military governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 安重誨死，復召延光與趙延壽並為樞密使。

translations.literal: When An Chonghui died, Yanguang was again summoned, and he and Zhao Yanshou were made Privy Commissioners together.
translations.idiomatic: After An Chonghui died, he was recalled and served with Zhao Yanshou as Privy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明宗問延光馬數幾何，對曰「騎軍三萬五千。

translations.literal: Mingzong asked Yanguang how many horses there were; he answered: "Thirty-five thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong asked how many horses the army had. "Thirty-five thousand cavalry," Yanguang replied.

sentences.zh: 」明宗撫髀嘆曰：「吾兵間四十年，自太祖在太原時，馬數不過七千，莊宗取河北，與梁家戰河上，馬才萬匹。

translations.literal: " Mingzong stroked his thigh and sighed: "I have been in arms forty years. When Taizu was at Taiyuan, horses numbered no more than seven thousand; when Zhuangzong took Hebei and fought Liang on the river, horses were barely ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong slapped his thigh and sighed. "Forty years in arms! When Taizu was at Taiyuan we had barely seven thousand horses. When Zhuangzong took Hebei and fought Liang on the river we had only ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 今有馬三萬五千而不能一天下，吾老矣，馬多奈何！

translations.literal: Now there are thirty-five thousand horses yet we cannot unify the realm. I am old—what good are so many horses!
translations.idiomatic: Now we have thirty-five thousand and still cannot unite the realm. I am old—what good are all these horses?

sentences.zh: 」延光因曰：「臣嘗計，一馬之費，可養步卒五人，三萬五千匹馬，十五萬兵之食也。

translations.literal: " Yanguang then said: "Your servant once calculated: the cost of one horse can feed five foot soldiers. Thirty-five thousand horses are the rations of a hundred fifty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanguang added: "I once reckoned that one horse costs as much as five foot soldiers. Thirty-five thousand horses feed an army of a hundred fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「肥戰馬而瘠吾人，此吾所愧也！」

translations.literal: " Mingzong said: "Fat war-horses and lean people—this is what I am ashamed of!"
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong said: "Fat horses and starving soldiers—that is what shames me!"

sentences.zh: 夏州李仁福卒，其子彜超自立而邀旄節。

translations.literal: Li Renfu of Xia prefecture died; his son Yichao set himself up and sought the commander's baton and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Renfu of Xia died, his son Yichao seized power and demanded the commission.

sentences.zh: 明宗遣安從進代之，彜超不受代。

translations.literal: Mingzong sent An Congjin to replace him; Yichao would not accept relief.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent An Congjin to replace him, but Yichao refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 以兵攻之，久不克。

translations.literal: Troops were sent to attack him; for long they could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The army besieged him for a long time without success.

sentences.zh: 隰州刺史劉遂凝馳驛入見獻策，言綏、銀二州之人，皆有內向之意，請除二刺史以招降之。

translations.literal: Liu Suining, prefect of Xi, galloped by post-horse to audience and offered a plan, saying the people of Sui and Yin prefectures all had intent to turn inward, and asking that two prefects be appointed to summon their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Suining, prefect of Xi, raced to court by post horse. He said the people of Sui and Yin were ready to defect and urged that two new prefects be appointed to win them over.

sentences.zh: 延光曰：「王師問罪，本在彜超，夏州已破，綏、銀豈足顧哉！

translations.literal: Yanguang said: "The imperial army's punitive mission aims at Yichao in the first place. Once Xia prefecture is broken, what need to care for Sui and Yin!
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang objected: "The campaign targets Yichao. Once Xia falls, what need is there to fuss over Sui and Yin?

sentences.zh: 若不破夏州，雖得綏、銀，不能守也。

translations.literal: If Xia prefecture is not broken, even if Sui and Yin are gained they cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: Without taking Xia, even if we gain Sui and Yin we cannot hold them.

sentences.zh: 」遂凝又請自馳入說彜超使出降，延光曰：「一遂凝，萬一失之不足惜，所惜者朝廷大體也。

translations.literal: " Suining again asked to ride in himself and persuade Yichao to surrender. Yanguang said: "One Suining—if by chance he fails, that is not worth grieving; what is worth grieving is the court's larger propriety.
translations.idiomatic: " Suining then asked to ride in and persuade Yichao to surrender in person. Yanguang said: "One Suining is expendable if he fails. What matters is the dignity of the court.

sentences.zh: 」是時，王淑妃用事，遂凝兄弟與淑妃有舊，方倚以蒙恩寵，所言無不聽，而大臣以妃故，多不敢爭，獨延光從容沮止之。

translations.literal: " At that time Consort Wang Shufei held power; Suining's brothers were old associates of the consort and were relying on her to win favor—whatever they said was heeded. Great ministers, because of the consort, mostly dared not dispute; only Yanguang calmly dissuaded them.
translations.idiomatic: " Consort Wang Shufei held sway at court. Suining's brothers were her old friends and won every argument through her favor. Most ministers dared not oppose them—only Yanguang quietly held his ground.

sentences.zh: 明宗有疾，不能視朝，京師之人，洶洶異議，藏竄山谷，或寄匿於軍營，有司不能禁。

translations.literal: Mingzong fell ill and could not hold court; people of the capital buzzed with wild talk, hid in mountain valleys, or lodged secretly in army camps—the authorities could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong fell ill and could not hold court, rumor swept the capital. People hid in the hills or took shelter in army camps, and the authorities could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 或勸延光以嚴法制之，延光曰：「制動當以靜，宜少待之。

translations.literal: Some urged Yanguang to restrain them with harsh law; Yanguang said: "To control unrest one should use calm—it is better to wait a little.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged harsh measures. Yanguang said: "Restlessness is best met with calm. Wait a little.

sentences.zh: 」已而明宗疾少間，京師乃定。

translations.literal: " Before long Mingzong's illness eased somewhat and the capital settled.
translations.idiomatic: " When Mingzong's health improved slightly, the capital quieted down.

sentences.zh: 是時，秦王握兵驕甚，宋王弱而且在外，議者多屬意於潞王。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qin held troops and was very arrogant; the Prince of Song was weak and moreover abroad—many in council looked to the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin held the armies and grew insolent. The Prince of Song was weak and far from court. Many looked to the Prince of Lu instead.

sentences.zh: 延光懼禍之及也，乃求罷去。

translations.literal: Yanguang feared disaster would reach him and asked to resign and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would be swept up in the coming disaster, Yanguang asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 延壽陰察延光有避禍意，亦遽求罷。

translations.literal: Yanshou secretly observed that Yanguang wished to avoid disaster and also hurried to ask to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou sensed Yanguang's fear and hurried to resign as well.

sentences.zh: 明宗再三留之，二人辭益懇至，繼之以泣。

translations.literal: Mingzong repeatedly tried to keep them; the two men's resignations grew all the more earnest, followed by weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong urged them to stay again and again. They pleaded all the more earnestly, weeping as they spoke.

sentences.zh: 明宗不得已，乃皆罷之，延光復鎮成德，而用朱弘昭、馮赟為樞密使。

translations.literal: Mingzong had no choice and dismissed them both; Yanguang returned to govern Chengde, and Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun were made Privy Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had no choice but to let them go. Yanguang returned to Chengde, and Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun became Privy Commissioners.

sentences.zh: 已而秦王舉兵見誅，明宗崩，潞王反，殺湣帝，唐室大亂，弘昭、赟皆及禍以死。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Qin raised troops and was executed; Mingzong died; the Prince of Lu rebelled, killed the Lamented Emperor, and Tang fell into great disorder—Hongzhao and Yun both met disaster and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Qin rebelled and was executed. Mingzong died. The Prince of Lu rose, killed the Lamented Emperor, and Tang plunged into chaos. Hongzhao and Yun both died in the upheaval.

sentences.zh: 末帝復詔延光為樞密使，拜宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor again ordered Yanguang as Privy Commissioner and appointed him military governor of Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor recalled Yanguang as Privy Commissioner and made him military governor of Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 天雄軍亂，逐節度使劉延皓，遣延光討平之，即以為天雄軍節度使。

translations.literal: Tianxiong army mutinied, drove out military governor Liu Yanhao, and Yanguang was sent to pacify it; he was then made military governor of Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxiong mutinied and drove out Liu Yanhao, Yanguang was sent to pacify the army and was made its military governor.

sentences.zh: 有平山人秘瓊者，為成德軍節度使董溫其衙內指揮使，後溫其為契丹所虜，瓊乃悉殺溫其家族，瘞之一穴，而取其家貲巨萬計，晉高祖入立，以瓊為齊州防禦使，橐其貲裝，道出於魏。

translations.literal: There was a man of Pingshan named Mi Qiong who had been inner-palace commander under Chengde military governor Dong Wenqi. Later Wenqi was captured by Khitan; Qiong then killed Wenqi's entire clan, buried them in one pit, and took his household wealth, reckoned in the tens of thousands. When Jin's Gaozu entered and took the throne, he made Qiong defensive commissioner of Qi prefecture. Qiong packed his wealth and passed through Wei on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Qiong of Pingshan had been inner-palace commander to Dong Wenqi of Chengde. When Khitan captured Wenqi, Qiong slaughtered his entire clan, buried them in one pit, and seized a fortune. Jin Gaozu made him defensive commissioner of Qi. He loaded his wealth and passed through Wei on the road.

sentences.zh: 延光陰遣人以書招之，瓊不納，延光怒，選兵伏境上，伺瓊過，殺之於夏津，悉取其貲，以戍邏者誤殺聞。

translations.literal: Yanguang secretly sent someone with a letter to win him over; Qiong would not accept. Yanguang was angry, chose troops and hid them on the border, waited for Qiong to pass, killed him at Xiajin, took all his wealth, and reported it as border patrols mistakenly killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang secretly tried to win him with a letter. Qiong refused. Enraged, Yanguang ambushed him at the border, killed him at Xiajin, seized everything he carried, and reported it as a border patrol's mistake.

sentences.zh: 由是高祖疑其必為亂，乃幸汴州。

translations.literal: From this Gaozu suspected he would surely rebel and then traveled to Bian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu suspected rebellion was coming and traveled to Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 天福二年六月，延光遂反，遣其牙將孫銳、澶州刺史馮暉，以兵二萬距黎陽，掠滑、衛。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianfu, Yanguang then rebelled, sending his牙 general Sun Rui and Cang prefect Feng Hui with twenty thousand troops to hold Liyang and plunder Hua and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianfu 2, Yanguang rebelled. He sent Sun Rui and Feng Hui of Cang with twenty thousand men to hold Liyang and raid Hua and Wei.

sentences.zh: 高祖以楊光遠為招討使，引兵自滑州渡胡梁攻之。

translations.literal: Gaozu made Yang Guangyuan pacification commissioner and led troops from Hua prefecture across Hubian to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made Yang Guangyuan pacification commissioner and led troops from Huazhou across Hubian to attack him.

sentences.zh: 銳輕脫無謀，兵行以娼女十餘自隨，張蓋操扇，酣歌飲食自若。

translations.literal: Rui was frivolous and without strategy; on the march he took more than ten courtesans with him, spread canopies and waved fans, and sang and drank at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was reckless and witless. On the march he brought a dozen courtesans, raised canopies, waved fans, and feasted as if at leisure.

sentences.zh: 軍士苦大熱，皆不為用。

translations.literal: The soldiers suffered from great heat and would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers sweltered in the heat and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 光遠得諜者，詢得其謀，誘銳等渡河，半濟而擊之，兵多溺死，銳、暉退走入魏，閉壁不復出。

translations.literal: Guangyuan obtained a spy, questioned him and learned their plan, lured Rui and the others to cross the river, and struck them halfway across—many troops drowned. Rui and Hui retreated into Wei, shut the walls, and did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan captured a spy, learned their plans, and lured Rui across the river. He struck halfway across; many drowned. Rui and Hui fled into Wei, shut the gates, and would not come out again.

sentences.zh: 初，延光反意未決，而得暴疾不能興，銳乃陰召暉入城。

translations.literal: At first Yanguang's intent to rebel was not yet settled when he fell suddenly ill and could not rise; Rui then secretly summoned Hui into the city.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yanguang had not fully decided to rebel when a sudden illness laid him low. Rui secretly summoned Hui into the city.

sentences.zh: 迫延光反，延光惶惑，遂從之。

translations.literal: They forced Yanguang to rebel; bewildered, he followed them.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him to rebel. Dazed and helpless, he went along.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞延光用銳等以反，笑曰：「吾雖不武，然嘗從明宗取天下，攻堅破強多矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard Yanguang had used Rui and the others to rebel and laughed: "Though I am not martial, I once followed Mingzong to take the realm and have many times stormed strongholds and broken powerful foes.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard Yanguang had rebelled with Rui and the rest, he laughed. "I may not be a great warrior, but I followed Mingzong across the realm and broke many a strong foe.

sentences.zh: 如延光已非我敵，況銳等兒戲邪？

translations.literal: If even Yanguang is no longer my match, how much less Rui and the others—child's play!
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang alone is no match for me—what are Rui and his crew but children at play?

sentences.zh: 行取孺子爾！

translations.literal: I am about to take these infants!
translations.idiomatic: I will scoop them up like children!

sentences.zh: 」乃決意討之。

translations.literal: " He then resolved to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: " He resolved to crush them.

sentences.zh: 延光初無必反意，及銳等敗，延光遣牙將王知新賫表自歸，高祖不見，以知新屬武德司。

translations.literal: At first Yanguang had no settled intent to rebel; when Rui and the others were defeated, Yanguang sent his牙 general Wang Zhixin bearing a memorial to surrender himself. Gaozu would not receive him and handed Zhixin over to the Bureau of Martial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang had never fully meant to rebel. After Rui's defeat he sent Wang Zhixin with a memorial offering surrender. Gaozu refused to see him and handed Zhixin over to the Bureau of Martial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 延光又附楊光遠表請降，不報，延光遂堅守。

translations.literal: Yanguang again appended Yang Guangyuan's memorial requesting surrender; there was no reply, and Yanguang then held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang sent another memorial through Yang Guangyuan begging to surrender. No answer came, and he held the city.

sentences.zh: 晉以箭書二百射城中，悉赦魏人，募能斬延光者。

translations.literal: Jin shot two hundred arrow-messages into the city, pardoning all men of Wei and offering reward to whoever could kill Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin rained two hundred messages on arrows into the city, pardoning every man of Wei and promising reward for Yanguang's head.

sentences.zh: 然魏城堅難下，攻之逾年不克，師老糧匱。

translations.literal: Yet Wei's walls were strong and hard to take; they attacked more than a year without success—the army grew weary and provisions ran out.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's walls were too strong. The siege dragged on more than a year without success; the army tired and grain ran out.

sentences.zh: 宗正丞石帛上書極諫，請赦延光，願以單車入說而降之。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau Shi Bo submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance, asking that Yanguang be pardoned and offering to go alone in a single carriage to persuade him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bo of the Imperial Clan Bureau submitted a fierce memorial urging pardon for Yanguang and offering to ride alone into the city to talk him down.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦悔悟。

translations.literal: Gaozu also came to regret and understand.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu too repented.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，使謁者入魏赦延光，延光乃降，冊封東平郡王、天平軍節度使，賜鐵券。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year he sent an envoy into Wei to pardon Yanguang; Yanguang then surrendered and was enfeoffed Prince of Dongping and military governor of Tianping, and granted an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 3 he sent an envoy to pardon Yanguang. Yanguang surrendered, was enfeoffed Prince of Dongping and military governor of Tianping, and received an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 居數月來朝，因慚請老，以太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: After several months he came to court; ashamed, he asked to retire on grounds of age and was dismissed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he came to court, begged to retire in shame, and was dismissed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖赦降延光，語使者謂之曰：「許卿不死矣，若降而殺之，何以享國？

translations.literal: When Gaozu first pardoned the surrendered Yanguang, he told the envoy: "I promise you shall not die. If I kill you after you surrender, how could I hold the realm?
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first pardoned him, he told the envoy: "I promise you will not die. If I kill you after you surrender, how can I rule the realm?

sentences.zh: 」延光謀於副使李式，式曰：「主上敦信明義，許之不死，則不死矣。

translations.literal: " Yanguang consulted his deputy Li Shi; Shi said: "Our lord is earnest in faith and clear in righteousness. If he promises you shall not die, then you shall not die.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanguang asked his deputy Li Shi. Shi said: "The emperor is a man of his word. If he promises you life, you will live.

sentences.zh: 」乃降。

translations.literal: " He then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " So he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 乃致仕居京師，歲時宴見，高祖待之與群臣無間，然心不欲使在京師。

translations.literal: He then retired and lived in the capital; at the seasonal feasts he was received in audience, and Gaozu treated him no differently from the other ministers—yet in his heart he did not wish Yanguang to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to the capital and was received at court like any minister, but Gaozu did not want him there.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，使宣徽使劉處讓載酒夜過延光，謂曰：「上遣處讓來時，適有契丹使至，北朝皇帝問晉魏博反臣何在，恐晉不能制，當鎖以來，免為中國後患。

translations.literal: After more than a year he sent Palace Commissioner Liu Churang with wine to visit Yanguang by night and said: "When the emperor sent Churang, a Khitan envoy had just arrived. The northern emperor asked where Jin's rebel from Weibo was, fearing Jin could not control him and wishing him chained and brought north lest he become a later trouble for China.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he sent Liu Churang with wine by night. Churang said: "The Khitan envoy just asked where your Weibo rebel is. He fears Jin cannot control you and wants you taken north in chains.

sentences.zh: 」延光聞之泣下，莫知所為。

translations.literal: " Hearing this, Yanguang wept and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanguang wept, helpless.

sentences.zh: 處讓曰：「當且之洛陽，以避契丹使者。

translations.literal: Churang said: "For now you should go to Luoyang to avoid the Khitan envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Churang said: "Go to Luoyang for now to avoid the envoy.

sentences.zh: 」延光曰：「楊光遠留守河南，吾之仇也。

translations.literal: " Yanguang said: "Yang Guangyuan holds Henan—he is my enemy.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanguang said: "Yang Guangyuan holds Henan—my enemy.

sentences.zh: 吾有田宅在河陽，可以往乎？

translations.literal: I have fields and houses at Heyang—may I go there?
translations.idiomatic: I have estates at Heyang—may I go there?

sentences.zh: 」處讓曰：「可也。

translations.literal: " Churang said: "You may.
translations.idiomatic: " "You may."

sentences.zh: 」乃挈其帑歸河陽。

translations.literal: " He then took his household and returned to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He took his household to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 其行輜重盈路，光遠利其貲，果圖之。

translations.literal: His baggage train filled the road; Guangyuan coveted his wealth and indeed plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: His train filled the road. Guangyuan coveted his wealth and plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 因奏曰：「延光反覆奸臣，若不圖之，非北走胡則南走吳越，請拘之洛陽。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Yanguang is a treacherous minister who turns again and again. If we do not deal with him, he will flee north to the barbarians or south to Wu and Yue—please detain him in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Yanguang is a traitor who turns coat at every chance. Unless we act, he will flee north to the Khitan or south to Wu and Yue. Detain him in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 」高祖猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Gaozu hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu hesitated.

sentences.zh: 光遠兼鎮河陽，其子承勛知州事，乃遣承勛以兵脅之使自裁。

translations.literal: Guangyuan also held Heyang; his son Chengxun governed the prefecture and sent Chengxun with troops to force Yanguang to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan also held Heyang. His son Chengxun governed there and sent troops to force Yanguang to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 延光曰：「天子賜我鐵券，許之不死，何得及此？

translations.literal: Yanguang said: "The Son of Heaven granted me an iron certificate and promised I should not die—how can it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang cried: "The emperor gave me an iron certificate and promised I would not die—how can this be?

sentences.zh: 」乃以壯士驅之上馬，行至浮橋，推墮水溺死，以延光自投水死聞，因盡取其貲。

translations.literal: Strong men drove him onto a horse; reaching the floating bridge they pushed him into the water and he drowned. It was reported that Yanguang had thrown himself into the water, and they took all his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: They forced him onto a horse, pushed him from the bridge into the river, and drowned him. They reported suicide and seized everything he owned.

sentences.zh: 高祖以適會其意，不問，為之輟朝，贈太傅。

translations.literal: Gaozu, since it suited his wish, made no inquiry, suspended court in mourning, and posthumously appointed him Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, pleased at the outcome, asked no questions, suspended court, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 水運軍使曹千獲其流屍於繆家灘，詔許歸葬相州。

translations.literal: Water-transport commissioner Cao Qian recovered his floating corpse at Miaojia Ford; an edict permitted burial in Xiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Qian of the water transport service recovered his body at Miaojia Ford. An edict allowed burial in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 已葬，墓輒崩，破其棺槨，頭顱皆碎。

translations.literal: After burial the tomb repeatedly collapsed; the coffin was broken open and the skull shattered.
translations.idiomatic: After burial the tomb collapsed again and again. The coffin was opened and the skull shattered.

sentences.zh: 初，秘瓊殺董溫其取其貲，延光又殺瓊而取之，而終以貲為光遠所殺，而光遠亦不能免也。

translations.literal: Earlier Mi Qiong had killed Dong Wenqi and taken his wealth; Yanguang killed Qiong and took it; in the end he was killed for his wealth by Guangyuan—and Guangyuan too could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Qiong had killed Dong Wenqi for his wealth; Yanguang killed Qiong and took it; in the end Guangyuan killed Yanguang for the same wealth—and Guangyuan too could not escape.

sentences.zh: 當延光反時，有李彥珣者，為河陽行軍司馬，張從賓反河陽，彥珣附之，從賓敗，彥珣奔於魏，延光以為步軍都監，使之守城。

translations.literal: When Yanguang rebelled there was a Li Yanxun who served as marching army marshal of Heyang. Zhang Congbin rebelled at Heyang; Yanxun joined him. When Congbin was defeated Yanxun fled to Wei; Yanguang made him chief inspector of the foot army and had him defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanguang rebelled, Li Yanxun was marching army marshal of Heyang. He joined Zhang Congbin's rebellion there. When Congbin fell, Yanxun fled to Wei. Yanguang made him chief foot inspector and put him in charge of the walls.

sentences.zh: 招討使楊光遠知彥珣邢州人也，其母尚在，乃遣人之邢州，取其母至城下，示彥珣以招之，彥珣望見，自射殺之。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Yang Guangyuan knew Yanxun was a man of Xing prefecture and that his mother was still alive; he sent men to Xing, brought his mother below the walls, and showed her to Yanxun to win him over. Yanxun saw her and shot her dead himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan knew Yanxun was from Xingzhou and that his mother still lived. He brought her below the walls to sway him. Yanxun saw her and shot her dead with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 及延光出降，晉高祖拜彥珣房州刺史，大臣言彥珣殺母當誅，高祖以謂赦令已行，不可失信。

translations.literal: When Yanguang surrendered, Jin Gaozu appointed Yanxun prefect of Fang. Great ministers said that killing one's mother deserved execution; Gaozu said the amnesty had already been proclaimed and faith could not be broken.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanguang surrendered, Gaozu made Yanxun prefect of Fang. Ministers said he deserved death for killing his mother. Gaozu said the amnesty was already in force and could not be revoked.

sentences.zh: 後以坐贓誅。

translations.literal: Later he was executed for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was executed for embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，甚哉，人性之慎於習也！

translations.literal: Alas, how deep is human nature's caution toward habit!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how deeply habit shapes human nature!

sentences.zh: 故聖人於仁義深矣，其為教也，勤而不怠，緩而不迫，欲民漸習而自趨之，至於久而安以成俗也。

translations.literal: Thus the sages made benevolence and righteousness profound; in teaching they were diligent without slackening, gentle without forcing, wishing the people to grow used to it by degrees and of themselves incline toward it, until after long time they rested in it and custom was formed.
translations.idiomatic: The sages made benevolence and righteousness profound. They taught diligently but without haste, gently but without slack, so that people might grow used to goodness by degrees until custom itself carried them.

sentences.zh: 然民之無知，習見善則安於為善，習見惡則安於為惡。

translations.literal: Yet the people are without knowledge: accustomed to seeing good they rest in doing good; accustomed to seeing evil they rest in doing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Yet people are ignorant: show them good and they settle into good; show them evil and they settle into evil.

sentences.zh: 五代之亂，其來遠矣。

translations.literal: The disorder of the Five Dynasties came from far back.
translations.idiomatic: The chaos of the Five Dynasties had deep roots.

sentences.zh: 自唐之衰，干戈饑饉，父不得育其子，子不得養其親。

translations.literal: From Tang's decline, war and famine—fathers could not rear their sons, sons could not support their parents.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang's fall came war and famine. Fathers could not raise sons; sons could not care for parents.

sentences.zh: 其始也，骨肉不能相保，蓋出於不幸，因之禮義日以廢，恩愛日以薄，其習久而遂以大壞，至於父子之間，自相賊害。

translations.literal: At the beginning, flesh and blood could not protect one another—mostly from misfortune; then ritual and righteousness daily decayed, affection daily thinned; the habit long endured and at last was greatly ruined, until between father and son they harmed one another.
translations.idiomatic: At first kin could not protect one another—mostly from sheer misfortune. Then ritual decayed and love thinned day by day until habit rotted everything, and fathers and sons turned on each other.

sentences.zh: 五代之際，其禍害不可勝道也。

translations.literal: In the age of the Five Dynasties the harm cannot be told to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties the harm is beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 夫人情莫不共知愛其親，莫不共知惡於不孝，然彥珣彎弓射其母，高祖從而赦之，非徒彥珣不自知為大惡，而高祖亦安焉不以為怪也，豈非積習之久而至於是歟！

translations.literal: There is nothing in human feeling that does not alike know love for one's kin, nothing that does not alike detest unfilial conduct—yet Yanxun bent his bow and shot his mother, and Gaozu followed by pardoning him. It was not only that Yanxun did not know it as great evil, but Gaozu too rested in it and was not struck as strange—was it not accumulated habit long enduring that brought matters to this!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone loves his kin and hates unfilial acts—yet Yanxun shot his mother and Gaozu pardoned him. Yanxun scarcely knew it as monstrous; Gaozu scarcely thought it strange. Had habit not rotted them for generations?

sentences.zh: 《語》曰：「性相近，習相遠。

translations.literal: The Analects says: "By nature men are near alike; by habit they diverge far.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: "By nature we are alike; by habit we diverge.

sentences.zh: 」至其極也，使人心不若禽獸，可不哀哉！

translations.literal: " At the extreme, it makes men's hearts fall below beasts—how is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: " At the extreme, the heart falls below the beasts. How pitiful!

sentences.zh: 若彥珣之惡，而恬然不以為怪，則晉出帝之絕其父，宜其舉世不知為非也。

translations.literal: If Yanxun's evil could be taken calmly and not thought strange, then when Jin's Deposed Emperor cut off his father, it was fitting that all the world did not know it as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: If Yanxun's crime could pass without shock, it is no wonder that when Jin's Deposed Emperor abandoned his father, the world saw no wrong in it.

sentences.zh: 婁繼英

translations.literal: Lou Jiying
translations.idiomatic: Lou Jiying

sentences.zh: 婁繼英，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Lou Jiying—his place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Jiying's origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 歷梁、唐，為絳、冀二州刺史、北面水陸轉運使、耀州團練使。

translations.literal: Through Liang and Tang he was prefect of Jiang and Ji, commissioner of northern land and water transport, and regimental trainer of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Through Liang and Tang he served as prefect of Jiang and Ji, commissioner of northern transport, and regimental trainer of Yao.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，為左監門衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he was general of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Gaozu he was general of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 繼英子婦，溫延沼女也，自明宗時誅其父韜，延沼兄弟廢居於許，心常怨望。

translations.literal: Jiying's son's wife was the daughter of Wen Yanhao; from Mingzong's time his father Tao had been executed, and the Yanhao brothers lived in disgrace at Xu, hearts always resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Jiying's daughter-in-law was Wen Yanhao's daughter. Since Mingzong had executed her father Tao, the Yanhao brothers lived in disgrace at Xu, nursing resentment.

sentences.zh: 及範延光反，繼英有弟為魏州子城都虞候，延光遣人以蠟書招繼英，繼英乃遣延沼入魏見延光，延光大喜，與之信箭，使陰圖許。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang rebelled, Jiying had a younger brother who was chief adjutant of Wei's inner citadel; Yanguang sent someone with a wax-sealed letter to win Jiying, and Jiying sent Yanhao into Wei to see Yanguang. Yanguang was greatly pleased, gave him a trust-arrow, and had him secretly plot Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang rebelled, Jiying's brother was chief adjutant of Wei's inner citadel. Yanguang sent a wax-sealed letter. Jiying sent Yanhao to Wei. Yanguang rejoiced, gave him a trust-arrow, and set him to plot Xu.

sentences.zh: 延沼與其弟延浚、延袞募不逞之徒千人，期以攻許。

translations.literal: Yanhao with his brothers Yanjun and Yangun recruited a thousand unruly men, fixing a date to attack Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhao and his brothers Yanjun and Yangun recruited a thousand desperadoes and fixed a day to strike Xu.

sentences.zh: 而許州節度使萇從簡以延光之反，疑有應者，為備甚嚴。

translations.literal: Xu military governor Chang Congjian, because of Yanguang's rebellion, suspected there were sympathizers and made preparations very strict.
translations.idiomatic: Xu prefect Chang Congjian, suspecting collusion after Yanguang's revolt, fortified the city strictly.

sentences.zh: 延沼未及發，延光蠟書事泄於京師，繼英惶恐不自安，乃出奔許。

translations.literal: Before Yanhao could move, Yanguang's wax letter was exposed at the capital; Jiying was terrified and fled to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could move, the wax letter was exposed at court. Jiying fled in terror to Xu.

sentences.zh: 高祖下詔招慰之，使復位，繼英懼不敢出。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued an edict summoning and comforting him, telling him to resume his post; Jiying feared and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu issued an edict summoning and reassuring him, but Jiying was too afraid to emerge.

sentences.zh: 溫氏兄弟謀殺繼英以自歸，延沼以其女故不忍。

translations.literal: The Wen brothers plotted to kill Jiying to surrender themselves; Yanhao could not bear it because of his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Wen brothers plotted to kill Jiying to win pardon, but Yanhao spared him for his daughter's sake.

sentences.zh: 張從賓反於洛陽，延沼兄弟乃與繼英俱投從賓於汜水。

translations.literal: Zhang Congbin rebelled at Luoyang; the Yanhao brothers then joined Jiying in throwing themselves on Congbin at Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Congbin rebelled at Luoyang, the Wen brothers and Jiying joined him at Sishui.

sentences.zh: 繼英知溫氏之初欲殺己也，反譖延沼兄弟於從賓，從賓殺之。

translations.literal: Jiying knew the Wen family had first wished to kill him and in turn slandered the Yanhao brothers to Congbin; Congbin killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiying knew the Wens had meant to kill him and slandered the brothers to Congbin, who executed them.

sentences.zh: 從賓敗，繼英為杜重威所殺。

translations.literal: When Congbin was defeated, Jiying was killed by Du Chongwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Congbin fell, Du Chongwei killed Jiying.

sentences.zh: 安重榮

translations.literal: An Chongrong
translations.idiomatic: An Chongrong

sentences.zh: 重榮雖武夫，而曉吏事，其下不能欺。

translations.literal: Though Chongrong was a military man, he understood administrative affairs; those below him could not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong was a soldier, but he understood government; no subordinate could fool him.

sentences.zh: 有夫婦訟其子不孝者，重榮拔劍授其父，使自殺之，其父泣曰：「不忍也！

translations.literal: A couple sued their son for unfilial conduct; Chongrong drew his sword and gave it to the father, telling him to kill the son himself. The father wept: "I cannot bear it!
translations.idiomatic: A couple sued their son for unfilial conduct. Chongrong handed the father his sword and told him to kill the boy. The father wept: "I cannot!

sentences.zh: 」其母從傍詬罵，奪其劍而逐之，問之，乃繼母也，重榮叱其母出，後射殺之。

translations.literal: " The mother cursed from the side, seized the sword and drove him off; on inquiry she proved to be the stepmother. Chongrong drove the mother out and later shot her dead.
translations.idiomatic: " The mother cursed, seized the sword, and drove him off. She was the stepmother. Chongrong expelled her and later shot her dead.

sentences.zh: 重榮起於軍卒，暴至富貴，而見唐廢帝、晉高祖皆自藩侯得國，嘗謂人曰：「天子寧有種邪？

translations.literal: Chongrong rose from the ranks to sudden wealth and honor; seeing Tang's Deposed Emperor and Jin Gaozu both gain the realm from frontier posts, he once said to others: "Is there breed in a Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: A common soldier risen to riches, he saw Tang's Deposed Emperor and Jin Gaozu both seize the throne from the frontier. He said: "Are emperors born to the purple?

sentences.zh: 兵強馬壯者為之爾！

translations.literal: Whoever has strong troops and fine horses makes one!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever has the stronger army makes one!

sentences.zh: 」雖懷異志，而未有以發也。

translations.literal: " Though he harbored separate intent, he had no occasion to act.
translations.idiomatic: " He harbored ambition but had no opening.

sentences.zh: 是時，高祖與契丹約為父子，契丹驕甚，高祖奉之愈謹，重榮憤然，以謂「詘中國以尊夷狄，困已敝之民，而充無厭之欲，此晉萬世恥也！

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu had agreed with Khitan as father and son; Khitan grew very arrogant and Gaozu served them all the more carefully. Chongrong was indignant and said: "To bow China before honoring barbarians, to exhaust our worn people to fill insatiable desire—this is Jin's shame for ten thousand generations!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had sworn father-son ties with Khitan, who grew insolent while Gaozu bowed lower. Chongrong raged: "To humble China before barbarians and drain a weary people to feed endless greed—that is eternal shame for Jin!

sentences.zh: 」數以此非誚高祖。

translations.literal: He often reproached and mocked Gaozu for this.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked Gaozu again and again.

sentences.zh: 契丹使者往來過鎮州，重榮箕踞慢罵，不為之禮，或執殺之。

translations.literal: Khitan envoys passing through Zhen prefecture—Chongrong sat sprawled and reviled them without ceremony, and sometimes seized and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys passing through Zhenzhou he insulted sprawled on his seat, sometimes seizing and killing them.

sentences.zh: 是時，吐渾白氏役屬契丹，苦其暴虐，重榮誘之入塞。

translations.literal: At that time the Tuguhun of the Bai clan served Khitan and suffered their cruelty; Chongrong enticed them across the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuguhun Bai clan, subject to Khitan cruelty, he lured inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 契丹數遣使責高祖，並求使者，高祖對使者鞠躬俯首，受責愈謹，多為好辭以自解，而姑息重榮不能詰。

translations.literal: Khitan repeatedly sent envoys to reproach Gaozu and demand the envoys back; Gaozu bowed to the envoys and received the blame all the more carefully, mostly using fine words to excuse himself, and indulged Chongrong without pressing him.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys rebuked Gaozu and demanded his men back. Gaozu bowed and apologized, yet indulged Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 乃遣供奉官張澄以兵二千搜索並、鎮、忻、代山谷中吐渾，悉驅出塞。

translations.literal: He then sent palace attendant Zhang Cheng with two thousand troops to search the valleys of Bing, Zhen, Xin, and Dai for Tuguhun and drive them all beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Cheng with two thousand men to scour the valleys of Bing, Zhen, Xin, and Dai and drive the Tuguhun out.

sentences.zh: 吐渾去而復來，重榮卒納之，因招集亡命，課民種稗，食馬萬匹，所為益驕。

translations.literal: The Tuguhun left and returned; Chongrong at last received them, gathered fugitives, levied the people to plant broomcorn, fed ten thousand horses, and grew all the more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: They left and returned. Chongrong took them in, gathered outlaws, forced the people to plant broomcorn, kept ten thousand horses, and grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 因怒殺指揮使賈章，誣之以反。

translations.literal: In anger he killed commander Jia Zhang and slandered him as a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: In rage he killed commander Jia Zhang and accused him of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 章女尚幼，欲舍之，女曰：「吾家三十口皆死於兵，存者特吾與父爾，今父死，吾何忍獨生，願就死！

translations.literal: Zhang's daughter was still young; he wished to spare her. The girl said: "Thirty in my family have died by arms; only my father and I remain. Now my father is dead—how could I bear to live alone? I beg to die!
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was young. He meant to spare her. She said: "Thirty of my kin died by the sword; only my father and I remain. Now he is dead—how can I live? Let me die!

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: He then killed her.
translations.idiomatic: He killed her.

sentences.zh: 鎮人於是高賈女之烈，而知重榮之必敗也。

translations.literal: The people of Zhen therefore exalted the girl's fortitude and knew Chongrong must fall.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Zhen honored the girl's courage and knew Chongrong was doomed.

sentences.zh: 重榮既僭侈，以為金魚袋不足貴，刻玉為魚佩之。

translations.literal: Chongrong had grown extravagant and thought the golden-fish pouch not noble enough; he carved jade into fish and wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Growing extravagant, he thought the golden-fish pouch beneath him and wore fish carved from jade.

sentences.zh: 娶二妻，高祖因之並加封爵。

translations.literal: He took two wives; Gaozu accordingly ennobled them both.
translations.idiomatic: He took two wives, and Gaozu ennobled both.

sentences.zh: 天福六年夏，契丹使者拽剌過鎮，重榮侵辱之，拽剌言不遜，重榮怒，執拽剌，以輕騎掠幽州南境之民，處之博野。

translations.literal: In summer of the sixth year of Tianfu the Khitan envoy Zhuai passed through Zhen; Chongrong insulted him; Zhuai spoke insolently; Chongrong in anger seized Zhuai, raided the southern border of You with light cavalry, and settled the people at Boye.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of Tianfu 6 the Khitan envoy Zhuai passed through Zhen. Chongrong insulted him; Zhuai answered insolently; Chongrong seized him, raided southern You with light horse, and settled captives at Boye.

sentences.zh: 上表曰：「臣昨據熟吐渾白承福、赫連功德等領本族三萬餘帳自應州來奔，又據生吐渾、渾、契、兩突厥三部南北將沙陀、安慶、九府等各領其族、牛羊、車帳、甲馬七八路來奔，具言契丹殘害，掠取生口羊馬，自今年二月已後，號令諸蕃，點閱強壯，辦具軍裝，期以上秋南向。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Your servant yesterday received the settled Tuguhun Bai Chengfeng, Helian Gongde, and others leading more than thirty thousand tents of their clans from Ying prefecture to defect; also received the raw Tuguhun, Hun, Qi, and both Turkic tribes, north and south, with the Shatuo, Anqing, and nine prefectures each leading their clans, cattle, sheep, carts, armor, and horses in seven or eight columns to defect, all saying Khitan's cruelty in seizing people, sheep, and horses; from the second month of this year onward they ordered the various tribes to muster the strong, prepare military gear, and plan a southern campaign in early autumn.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial ran thousands of words: settled Tuguhun, raw Tuguhun, Turks, Shatuo, and others—tens of thousands of tents—had fled Khitan cruelty and would fight by autumn.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃部誠恐上天不祐，敗滅家族，願先自歸，其諸部勝兵眾可十萬。

translations.literal: The various tribes truly feared Heaven would not bless them and their clans would be destroyed; they wished to come over first; their fighting men number roughly a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They feared heaven's curse and came first; their warriors numbered a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 又據沿河党項、山前後逸越利諸族首領皆遣人送契丹所授告身、敕牒、旗幟來歸款，皆號泣告勞，願治兵甲以報怨。

translations.literal: Also, along the river the Tangut and the Yue and Li clan leaders before and behind the mountains all sent men bringing the patents, edicts, banners, and credentials Khitan had granted them to submit, all weeping and reporting their hardship, wishing to arm for revenge.
translations.idiomatic: River Tangut and mountain chiefs sent Khitan patents and banners, weeping for revenge.

sentences.zh: 又據朔州節度副使趙崇殺節度使劉山，以城來歸。

translations.literal: Also, Shuo deputy military governor Zhao Chong killed military governor Liu Shan and brought the city over.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo deputy Zhao Chong killed Liu Shan and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 竊以諸蕃不招呼而自至，朔州不攻伐而自歸，雖系人情，盡由天意。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that the various tribes came without being summoned, and Shuo surrendered without being attacked—though it lies in human feeling, it is wholly from Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes came unbidden; Shuo fell unstormed—human will, but heaven's sign.

sentences.zh: 又念陷蕃諸將等，本自勛勞，久居富貴，沒身虜塞，酷虐不勝，企足朝廷，思歸可諒，茍聞傳檄，必盡倒戈。

translations.literal: Also considering the generals trapped among the barbarians—they were men of merit, long in wealth and honor, ending their lives in the desert, suffering cruelty beyond bearing, craning toward the court in hope of return; if they heard a proclamation, they would surely turn their blades.
translations.idiomatic: Generals trapped beyond the passes would turn their blades at a single proclamation.

sentences.zh: 」其表數千言。

translations.literal: The memorial ran several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 又為書以遺朝廷大臣、四方藩鎮，皆以契丹可取為言。

translations.literal: He also wrote letters to court ministers and frontier governors everywhere, all saying Khitan could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to court ministers and governors everywhere that Khitan could be beaten.

sentences.zh: 高祖患之，為之幸鄴，報重榮曰：「前世與虜和親，皆所以為天下計，今吾以天下臣之，爾以一鎮抗之，大小不等，無自辱焉！

translations.literal: Gaozu was troubled, traveled to Ye for the matter, and replied to Chongrong: "Former ages made peace with the barbarians—all to serve the realm. Now I make the realm their subject while you resist with one commandery—great and small are unequal; do not disgrace yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu traveled to Ye and warned him: "Past emperors made peace with the barbarians for the realm's sake. I subject the realm to them while you resist with one province—you only shame yourself!

sentences.zh: 」重榮謂晉無如我何，反意乃決。

translations.literal: Chongrong thought Jin could do nothing to him and his intent to rebel was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong thought Jin helpless and resolved to rebel.

sentences.zh: 重榮雖以契丹為言，反陰遣人與幽州節度使劉晞相結。

translations.literal: Though Chongrong spoke against Khitan, in secret he sent men to join with You military governor Liu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Though he railed at Khitan, he secretly contacted You governor Liu Xi.

sentences.zh: 契丹亦利晉多事，幸重榮之亂，期兩敝之，欲因以窺中國，故不加怒於重榮。

translations.literal: Khitan too profited from Jin's many troubles and hoped Chongrong's disorder would wear both sides down, wishing thereby to spy on China; therefore they did not grow angry at Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan welcomed Jin's troubles, hoping Chongrong would wear both sides down so they might probe China—so they did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 重榮將反也，其母又以為不可，重榮曰：「為母卜之。

translations.literal: As Chongrong was about to rebel, his mother again said it could not be done; Chongrong said: "I will divine for Mother.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to rebel, his mother forbade it. He said: "Let me divine for you.

sentences.zh: 」指其堂下幡竿龍口仰射之，曰：「吾有天下則中之。

translations.literal: He pointed to the dragon mouth of the banner pole in his hall, shot upward, and said: "If I am to have the realm I will hit it.
translations.idiomatic: He shot at the dragon mouth on his hall banner and said: "If I am to rule, I will hit it.

sentences.zh: 」一發而中，其母乃許。

translations.literal: One shot struck true; his mother then consented.
translations.idiomatic: One arrow struck true; his mother consented.

sentences.zh: 饒陽令劉巖獻水鳥五色，重榮曰：「此鳳也。

translations.literal: Raoyang magistrate Liu Yan presented a five-colored water bird; Chongrong said: "This is a phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Raoyang magistrate Liu Yan presented a five-colored water bird. Chongrong said: "A phoenix.

sentences.zh: 」畜之後潭。

translations.literal: He kept it in the rear pool.
translations.idiomatic: He kept it in his rear pool.

sentences.zh: 又使人為大鐵鞭以獻，誑其民曰：「鞭有神，指人，人輒死。

translations.literal: He also had men make a great iron whip to present, deceiving the people: "The whip is divine; point at a man and he dies.
translations.idiomatic: He had a great iron whip made and told the people: "The whip is divine—point it at a man and he dies.

sentences.zh: 」號「鐵鞭郎君」，出則以為前驅。

translations.literal: They called him "Lord Iron Whip"; when he went out it went before him.
translations.idiomatic: They called him Lord Iron Whip; it went before him wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 鎮之城門抱關鐵胡人，無故頭自落，鐵胡，重榮小字，雖甚惡之，然不悟也。

translations.literal: At the city gate of Zhen the gate-keeping iron Hu men's heads fell off for no reason—"Iron Hu" was Chongrong's childhood name. Though he hated it, he did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Iron Hu gate guards' heads fell off for no reason—Iron Hu was Chongrong's childhood name. He hated the omen but did not understand.

sentences.zh: 其冬，安從進反襄陽，重榮聞之，乃亦舉兵。

translations.literal: That winter An Congjin rebelled at Xiangyang; hearing it, Chongrong also raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: That winter An Congjin rebelled at Xiangyang. Hearing it, Chongrong rose too.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鎮州大旱、蝗，重榮聚饑民數萬，驅以向鄴，聲言入覲。

translations.literal: That year Zhen suffered great drought and locusts; Chongrong gathered tens of thousands of starving people, drove them toward Ye, and proclaimed he was coming to court.
translations.idiomatic: That year drought and locusts ravaged Zhen. Chongrong gathered tens of thousands of the starving, drove them toward Ye, and claimed he was coming to court.

sentences.zh: 行至宗城破家堤，高祖遣杜重威朔之，兵已交，其將趙彥之與重榮有隙，臨陣卷旗以奔晉軍，其鎧甲鞍轡皆裝以銀，晉國不知其來降，爭殺而分之。

translations.literal: Reaching Pozhou at Pojia Embankment, Gaozu sent Du Chongwei to meet him; the armies had joined battle when his general Zhao Yanzhi, who had a grudge against Chongrong, furled his banner mid-array and fled to the Jin army. His armor and saddle were all fitted with silver; Jin did not know he was coming over and vied to kill and divide him.
translations.idiomatic: At Pojia Embankment, Du Chongwei met him in battle. General Zhao Yanzhi, who hated Chongrong, furled his banner and fled to Jin. His silver-trimmed armor fooled them—they thought him an enemy and tore him apart.

sentences.zh: 重榮聞彥之降晉，大懼，退入於輜重中，其兵二萬皆潰去。

translations.literal: Chongrong heard Yanzhi had surrendered to Jin and was greatly afraid; he withdrew into the baggage train, and his twenty thousand troops all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Yanzhi had gone over, Chongrong panicked and hid among the wagons. His twenty thousand men melted away.

sentences.zh: 是冬大寒，潰兵饑凍及見殺無孑遺，重榮獨與十餘騎奔還，以牛馬革為甲，驅州人守城以待。

translations.literal: That winter was bitterly cold; the scattered troops starved and froze or were killed until none survived. Chongrong alone with a dozen horsemen fled back, made armor of cattle and horse hides, and drove the people of the prefecture to hold the walls and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Winter was savage. The routed army starved and froze until none remained. Chongrong fled back with a dozen riders, armored his men in hides, and forced the townspeople to hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 重威兵至城下，重榮裨將自城西水碾門引官軍以入，殺守城二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Chongwei's army reached below the walls; Chongrong's deputy led government troops in through the western Water-Mill Gate, and more than twenty thousand defenders were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei arrived. A deputy led imperial troops in through the Water-Mill Gate and slaughtered more than twenty thousand defenders.

sentences.zh: 重榮以吐渾數百騎守牙城，重威使人擒之，斬首以獻，高祖禦樓受馘，命漆其首送於契丹。

translations.literal: Chongrong with several hundred Tuguhun cavalry held the headquarters compound; Chongwei sent men to seize him, beheaded him, and presented the head. Gaozu received it from the tower, ordered the head lacquered, and sent it to Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong held the headquarters with a few hundred Tuguhun horse. Chongwei captured him, beheaded him, and presented the head. Gaozu received it from the tower, had it lacquered, and sent it to Khitan.

sentences.zh: 改成德軍為順德，鎮州曰恒州，常山曰恒山云。

translations.literal: Chengde army was renamed Shunde; Zhen prefecture was called Heng prefecture, and Changshan was called Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde became Shunde; Zhen was renamed Heng, and Changshan Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 安從進

translations.literal: An Congjin
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin

sentences.zh: 高祖取天下不順，常以此慚，藩鎮多務，過為姑息，而藩鎮之臣，或不自安，或心慕高祖所為，謂舉可成事，故在位七年，而反者六起，從進最後反，然皆不免也。

translations.literal: Gaozu had gained the realm by irregular means and was often ashamed of it; the frontier commands had many affairs and he indulged them excessively, while their ministers were sometimes uneasy or admired what Gaozu had done and thought rebellion could succeed. Thus in seven years on the throne there were six rebellions; Congjin rebelled last, yet none escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had seized the throne by irregular means and was ashamed. He indulged the commands too much; their officers either feared for their lives or thought they could do as he had done. In seven years six rebellions rose—Congjin was the last, and none escaped.

sentences.zh: 自範延光反鄴，從進已畜異志，恃江為險，招集亡命，益置軍兵。

translations.literal: From the time Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye, Congjin had already harbored separate intent, trusting the river as a barrier, gathering fugitives, and increasing his troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye, Congjin already nursed rebellion, trusting the Yangzi barrier, gathering outlaws, and swelling his army.

sentences.zh: 南方貢輸道出襄陽者，多擅留之，邀遮商旅，皆黥以充軍。

translations.literal: Tribute from the south passing through Xiangyang he often detained; he waylaid merchants and branded them to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He seized southern tribute passing through Xiangyang, waylaid merchants, and branded them into his ranks.

sentences.zh: 與安重榮陰相結托，期為表裹。

translations.literal: He secretly joined with An Chongrong, pledging mutual support inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly allied with An Chongrong, each to support the other.

sentences.zh: 高祖患之，謀徙從進，使人謂曰：「東平王建立來朝，願還鄉里，已徙上黨。

translations.literal: Gaozu was troubled and planned to move Congjin, sending someone to say: "The Prince of Dongping has come to court wishing to return home and has already been moved to Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu tried to transfer him, saying: "The Prince of Dongping has come to court and returned home; Shangdang is open.

sentences.zh: 朕虛青州以待卿，卿誠樂行，朕即降制。

translations.literal: I have left Qing prefecture waiting for you; if you truly wish to go, I will issue the order at once.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou waits for you. If you are willing to go, I will issue the order.

sentences.zh: 」從進報曰：「移青州在漢江南，臣即赴任。

translations.literal: " Congjin replied: "If Qing is moved south of the Han River, your servant will take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: " Congjin replied: "Only if Qing lies south of the Han will I go.

sentences.zh: 」高祖亦優容之。

translations.literal: Gaozu also indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu indulged him.

sentences.zh: 其子弘超為宮苑副使，居京師，從進請賜告歸，遂不遣。

translations.literal: His son Hongchao was deputy commissioner of the palace parks and lived in the capital; Congjin asked leave to return home and was not sent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongchao served at court. Congjin asked to visit home and was refused.

sentences.zh: 王令謙、潘知麟者，皆從進牙將也，常從從進最久，知其必敗，切諫之。

translations.literal: Wang Lingqian and Pan Zhilin were both Congjin's personal generals, long with him, and knew he must fail—they remonstrated urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Wang Lingqian and Pan Zhilin, who had served him longest, warned he was doomed.

sentences.zh: 從進遣子弘超與令謙遊南山，酒酣，令人推墮崖死。

translations.literal: Congjin sent his son Hongchao with Lingqian to tour the southern hills; when they were drunk he had men push Lingqian off the cliff to his death.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hongchao and Lingqian to tour the southern hills, got them drunk, and had Lingqian pushed off a cliff.

sentences.zh: 天福六年，安重榮執殺契丹使者，反跡見，高祖為之幸鄴，鄭王重貴留守京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, An Chongrong seized and killed Khitan envoys and his rebellion showed; Gaozu traveled to Ye for the matter, and Prince of Zheng Chonggui held the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 6, Chongrong killed Khitan envoys and rebellion showed. Gaozu went to Ye; Prince of Zheng Chonggui held the capital.

sentences.zh: 宰相和凝曰：「陛下且北，從進必反，何以制之？

translations.literal: Chief minister He Ning said: "Your Majesty goes north—Congjin will surely rebel; how will you control him?
translations.idiomatic: He Ning said: "If you go north, Congjin will rebel. How will you stop him?

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「卿意奈何？

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "What is your thought?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked his plan.

sentences.zh: 」凝曰：「臣聞兵法，先人者奪人，願為空名宣敕十數通授鄭王，有急則命將以往。

translations.literal: Ning said: "Your servant has heard in military law that he who seizes the initiative seizes the enemy. I wish to prepare a dozen blank edicts for the Prince of Zheng; in emergency he may command generals to go.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Seize the initiative. Give Chonggui blank edicts to dispatch generals in an emergency.

sentences.zh: 」從進聞高祖北，遂殺知麟以反。

translations.literal: Congjin heard Gaozu had gone north and then killed Zhilin and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Gaozu had gone north, Congjin killed Zhilin and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 鄭王以空名敕授李建崇、郭金海等討之，從進引兵攻鄧州，不克，進至湖陽，遇建崇等，大駭，以為神速，復為野火所燒，遂大敗。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zheng gave blank edicts to Li Jianchong, Guo Jinhai, and others to campaign; Congjin led troops to attack Deng prefecture without success, advanced to Huyang, met Jianchong and the rest, was greatly alarmed thinking them miraculously swift, and was again burned by prairie fires—he was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui gave blank edicts to Li Jianchong and Guo Jinhai. Congjin attacked Deng without success, advanced to Huyang, met them in alarm, was burned by prairie fire, and was routed.

sentences.zh: 從進以數十騎奔還襄陽。

translations.literal: Congjin fled back to Xiangyang with several dozen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Xiangyang with a few dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣高行周圍之，逾年糧盡，從進自焚死。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Gao Xingzhou to besiege him; after more than a year grain was exhausted and Congjin burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Gao Xingzhou to besiege him. After a year, grain ran out and Congjin burned himself.

sentences.zh: 執其子弘受及其將佐四十三人送京師，高祖禦樓受俘，徇於市而斬之。

translations.literal: They seized his son Hongshou and forty-three officers and generals and sent them to the capital; Gaozu received the captives from the tower, displayed them in the market, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongshou and forty-three officers were sent to the capital. Gaozu received them from the tower and beheaded them in the market.

sentences.zh: 降襄陽為防禦，贈令謙忠州刺史，知麟順州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiangyang was reduced to a defensive command; Lingqian was posthumously made prefect of Zhong, Zhilin prefect of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang became a defensive command. Lingqian was posthumously made prefect of Zhong, Zhilin of Shun.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan

sentences.zh: 楊光遠，字德明，其父曰阿噔啜，蓋沙陀部人也。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan, style Deming—his father was named Adengchuo and was a man of the Shatuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan, courtesy name Deming, was the son of Adengchuo of the Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 光遠初名阿檀，為唐莊宗騎將，從周德威戰契丹於新州，折其一臂，遂廢不用。

translations.literal: Guangyuan's original name was Atan; he was a cavalry officer of Tang's Zhuangzong and followed Zhou Dewei against Khitan at Xin prefecture, breaking one arm, and was then discarded from use.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Atan, he was Zhuangzong's cavalry officer. Fighting Khitan at Xin with Zhou Dewei, he lost an arm and was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 久之，以為幽州馬步軍都指揮使，戍瓦橋關。

translations.literal: After long time he was made chief commander of You's horse and foot and garrisoned Wagong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he became chief commander of You's horse and foot and garrisoned Wagong Pass.

sentences.zh: 光遠為人病禿折臂，不通文字，然有辨智，長於吏事。

translations.literal: Guangyuan was afflicted with baldness and a broken arm, illiterate, yet he had discernment and was skilled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bald, one-armed, and illiterate, he was nonetheless shrewd and skilled in government.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，為媯、瀛、冀、易四州刺史，以治稱。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he was prefect of Jiao, Ying, Ji, and Yi—renowned for his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he governed Jiao, Ying, Ji, and Yi and was praised for his rule.

sentences.zh: 初，唐兵破王都於中山，得契丹大將荝剌等十餘人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tang's army defeated Wang Du at Zhongshan, they captured more than ten Khitan great generals including Cila.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang defeated Wang Du at Zhongshan, they captured Khitan generals including Cila.

sentences.zh: 已而契丹與中國通和，遣使者求荝剌等，明宗與大臣議，皆欲歸之，獨光遠不可，曰：「荝剌皆北狄善戰者，彼失之如去手足；

translations.literal: Later Khitan made peace with China and sent envoys requesting Cila and the rest; Mingzong consulted ministers—all wished to return them; only Guangyuan objected: "Cila and the rest are northern Di skilled in battle; to lose them is like losing hands and feet;
translations.idiomatic: Khitan sought their return. Ministers agreed; Guangyuan alone objected: "Cila and the rest are Khitan's best fighters—to lose them is to lose hands and feet;

sentences.zh: 且居此久，熟知中國事，歸之豈吾利也！

translations.literal: and having lived here long they know China's affairs well—what profit to us in sending them back!
