translations.idiomatic: having lived here long they know our ways—what good is sending them back?

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「蕃人重盟誓，已與吾好，豈相負也？

translations.literal: Mingzong said: "Barbarians value sworn oaths; they are already friendly with us—how could they betray us?
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said: "Barbarians honor oaths. They are our friends—how could they betray us?

sentences.zh: 」光遠曰：「臣恐後悔不及爾！

translations.literal: Guangyuan said: "Your servant fears you will regret it too late!
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan said: "You will regret it too late!

sentences.zh: 」明宗嘉其說，卒不遣荝剌等。

translations.literal: Mingzong praised his argument and at last did not send Cila and the rest back.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong praised him and kept Cila and the rest.

sentences.zh: 光遠自易州刺史拜振武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Guangyuan from Yi prefect was appointed military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: From Yi he was made military governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年，徙鎮中山，兼北面行營都虞候，禦契丹於雲、應之間。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he was moved to govern Zhongshan, also chief adjutant of the northern field army, opposing Khitan between Yun and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai 2 he governed Zhongshan and served as northern chief adjutant against Khitan between Yun and Ying.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖起太原，末帝以光遠佐張敬達為太原四面招討副使，為契丹所敗，退守晉安寨。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, the Last Emperor made Guangyuan deputy pacification commissioner under Zhang Jingda for the four-sided campaign against Taiyuan; they were defeated by Khitan and withdrew to hold Jin'an Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, the Last Emperor made Guangyuan Zhang Jingda's deputy. Khitan defeated them at Jin'an Stockade.

sentences.zh: 契丹圍之數月，人馬食盡，殺馬而食，馬盡，乃殺敬達出降。

translations.literal: Khitan besieged them for months until men and horses ate all provisions; they killed horses to eat, and when horses were gone they killed Jingda and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan besieged them until horses were eaten, then men, then they killed Jingda and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 耶律德光見之，靳曰：「爾輩大是惡漢兒。

translations.literal: Yelü Deguang saw them and sneered: "You lot are very wicked Han fellows.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang sneered: "You are wicked Han dogs.

sentences.zh: 」光遠與諸將初不知其誚己，猶為謙言以對，德光曰：「不用鹽酪，食一萬匹戰馬，豈非惡漢兒邪！

translations.literal: Guangyuan and the generals at first did not know he was mocking them and still answered humbly. Deguang said: "Without salt and curds you ate ten thousand war-horses—is that not being wicked Han fellows!
translations.idiomatic: They answered humbly, not knowing he mocked them. Deguang said: "You ate ten thousand horses without salt—is that not wicked?

sentences.zh: 」光遠等大慚伏，德光問曰：「懼否？

translations.literal: Guangyuan and the rest were greatly ashamed and prostrated themselves. Deguang asked: "Afraid?
translations.idiomatic: They prostrated themselves in shame. "Afraid?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「甚懼。

translations.literal: All said: "Very afraid.
translations.idiomatic: All said: "Very afraid.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「何懼？

translations.literal: He said: "Afraid of what?"
translations.idiomatic: "Of what?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「懼皇帝將入蕃。

translations.literal: They said: "Afraid the emperor will enter the barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: " "That you will take us into the steppe."

sentences.zh: 」德光曰：「吾國無土地官爵以居汝，汝等勉事晉。

translations.literal: Deguang said: "My state has no lands, offices, or fiefs to house you—do your best serving Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang said: "We have no lands for you—serve Jin faithfully.

sentences.zh: 」晉高祖以光遠為宣武軍節度使、侍衛馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Jin Gaozu made Guangyuan military governor of Xuanyi and chief commander of the palace horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made him military governor of Xuanyi and chief of palace horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 光遠進見，佯為悒悒之色，常如有所恨者，高祖疑其有所不足，使人問之，對曰：「臣於富貴無不足也，惟不及張生鐵死得其所，此常為愧爾！

translations.literal: When Guangyuan came to audience he feigned a gloomy air, always as if nursing some grievance; Gaozu suspected he felt slighted and sent to ask. He answered: "Your servant has no lack in wealth and honor—only that I did not die like Iron Zhang at the right place; this I am always ashamed of!
translations.idiomatic: At court he feigned gloom, as if slighted. Asked why, he said: "I lack nothing—only that I did not die like Iron Zhang. That shames me!

sentences.zh: 」由是高祖以為忠，頗親信之。

translations.literal: From this Gaozu thought him loyal and trusted him closely.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu took this for loyalty and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉馬少，括天下馬以佐軍，景延廣請取光遠前所借官馬三百匹，光遠怒曰：「此馬先帝賜我，安得復取，是疑我反也！

translations.literal: At that time Jin had few horses and gathered horses empire-wide for the army; Jing Yanguang asked to take the three hundred government horses Guangyuan had earlier borrowed. Guangyuan raged: "These horses the late emperor gave me—how can they be taken back? This is suspecting me of rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Jin needed horses. Jing Yanguang demanded three hundred Gaozu had lent him. Guangyuan raged: "The late emperor gave me those horses—this means you suspect rebellion!

sentences.zh: 」遂謀為亂。

translations.literal: He then plotted disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 而承祚自單州逃歸，出帝即以承祚為淄州刺史，遣使者賜以玉帶、御馬以慰安之，光遠益驕，乃反。

translations.literal: Chengxun fled back from Dan prefecture; the Deposed Emperor at once made Chengxun prefect of Zi and sent envoys with a jade belt and imperial horse to comfort him—Guangyuan grew all the more arrogant and then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun fled from Dan. The Deposed Emperor made him prefect of Zi and sent gifts—Guangyuan grew bolder and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 召契丹入寇，陷貝州。

translations.literal: He summoned Khitan to invade and took Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Khitan, who took Bei.

sentences.zh: 博州刺史周儒亦叛降契丹。

translations.literal: Bo prefect Zhou Ru also rebelled and surrendered to Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Bo prefect Zhou Ru also defected to Khitan.

sentences.zh: 是時，出帝與耶律德光相距澶、魏之間，鄆州觀察判官竇儀計事軍中，謀曰：「今不以重兵大將守博州渡，使儒得引契丹東過河與光遠合，則河南危矣！

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor and Yelü Deguang faced each other between Cang and Wei; Yan observation and judging officer Dou Yi plotted in the army: "If we do not hold the Bo crossing with a strong force and great general, Ru can lead Khitan east across the river to join Guangyuan—then Henan is in peril!
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi warned: "Unless we hold Bo crossing, Ru will bring Khitan east to join Guangyuan—and Henan falls.

sentences.zh: 」出帝乃遣李守貞、皇甫遇以兵萬人沿河而下。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor then sent Li Shouzhen and Huangfu Yu with ten thousand troops down the river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Shouzhen and Huangfu Yu with ten thousand men downriver.

sentences.zh: 儒果引契丹自馬家渡濟河，方築壘，守貞等急擊之，契丹大敗，遂與光遠隔絕。

translations.literal: Ru indeed led Khitan to cross at Majia Ford and was building a fort when Shouzhen and the rest pressed the attack; Khitan was greatly defeated and was cut off from Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ru crossed at Majia Ford. Shouzhen struck while he was building a fort. Khitan was routed and cut off from Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 德光聞河上兵大敗，與晉決戰戚城，亦敗。

translations.literal: Deguang heard the river army was greatly defeated and fought Jin's decisive battle at Qi City—he was defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang fought at Qi City after the river defeat—and lost again.

sentences.zh: 契丹已北，出帝復遣守貞、符彥卿東討，光遠嬰城固守，自夏至冬，城中人相食幾盡。

translations.literal: Khitan had gone north; the Deposed Emperor again sent Shouzhen and Fu Yanqing east to campaign. Guangyuan clung to the walls; from summer to winter the people in the city nearly ate one another up.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan withdrew. Shouzhen and Fu Yanqing besieged Guangyuan from summer to winter until the city nearly ate itself.

sentences.zh: 光遠北望契丹，稽首以呼德光曰：「皇帝誤光遠耶！

translations.literal: Guangyuan looked north toward Khitan, kowtowed and called to Deguang: "Has the emperor wronged Guangyuan!
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed north: "Emperor, have you wronged me?

sentences.zh: 」其子承勛等勸光遠出降，光遠曰：「我在代北時，嘗以紙錢祭天池，投之輒沒，人言我當作天子，宜且待時，毋輕議也。

translations.literal: His sons Chengxun and the rest urged Guangyuan to surrender. Guangyuan said: "When I was in northern Dai I once offered paper money at Heaven Pool—it sank at once; men said I was fated to be Son of Heaven. Better wait the time—do not speak lightly.
translations.idiomatic: His sons urged surrender. He said: "At Dai I cast paper money into Heaven Pool and it sank—men said I was fated to rule. Wait!

sentences.zh: 」承勛知不可，乃殺節度判官丘濤、親將杜延壽、楊瞻、白延祚等，劫光遠幽之，遣人奉表待罪。

translations.literal: Chengxun knew it could not be done, then killed military governor's aide Qiu Tao, close generals Du Yanshou, Yang Zhan, Bai Yanzuo, and the rest, seized Guangyuan and imprisoned him, and sent men with a memorial awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun knew it was hopeless, killed Qiu Tao and other officers, imprisoned Guangyuan, and sent a memorial of surrender.

sentences.zh: 承信、承祚皆詣闕自歸，而光遠亦上章請死。

translations.literal: Chengxin and Chengzuo both came to court to surrender themselves, and Guangyuan also submitted a memorial asking for death.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin and Chengzuo surrendered at court; Guangyuan asked to die.

sentences.zh: 出帝以其二子為侍衛將軍，賜光遠昭書，許以不死，群臣皆以為不可，乃敕李守貞便宜處置。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor made his two sons palace guard generals and granted Guangyuan an edict of assurance that he would not die; ministers all said it could not be done, and he ordered Li Shouzhen to dispose of him as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made his sons guard generals and promised Guangyuan life. Ministers objected; he told Shouzhen to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 守貞遣客省副使何延祚殺之於其家。

translations.literal: Shouzhen sent Guest Bureau deputy He Yanzuo to kill him in his house.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen sent He Yanzuo to kill him at home.

sentences.zh: 延祚至其第，光遠方閱馬於廄，延祚使一都將入謂之曰：「天使在門，欲歸報天子，未有以藉手。

translations.literal: Yanzuo reached his residence; Guangyuan was just inspecting horses in the stable. Yanzuo had a commander enter and tell him: "The envoy is at the gate and wishes to report to the Son of Heaven but has nothing to show for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzuo found him in the stable. An officer said: "The envoy needs something to bring the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」光遠曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: Guangyuan said: "What do you mean?
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan asked what he meant.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「願得大王頭爾！

translations.literal: He said: "I wish to have the great king's head!
translations.idiomatic: " "Your head," he said.

sentences.zh: 」光遠罵曰：「我有何罪？

translations.literal: Guangyuan cursed: "What crime have I?
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan cursed: "What crime have I?

sentences.zh: 昔我以晉安寨降契丹，使爾家世世為天子，我亦望以富貴終身，而反負心若此！

translations.literal: In the past when I surrendered Jin'an Stockade to Khitan I made your house Son of Heaven for generations; I too hoped to end my days in wealth and honor—yet you are so faithless!
translations.idiomatic: I surrendered Jin'an and made your house emperors—I hoped to die rich—and this is my reward!

sentences.zh: 」遂見殺，以病卒聞。

translations.literal: He was then killed; it was reported that he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed; they reported illness.

sentences.zh: 承勛事晉為鄭州防禦使，德光滅晉，使人召承勛至京師，責其劫父，臠而食之，乃以承信為平盧節度使。

translations.literal: Chengxun served Jin as defensive commissioner of Zheng; when Deguang destroyed Jin he summoned Chengxun to the capital, reproached him for seizing his father, cut his flesh and ate it, and then made Chengxin military governor of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun served Jin at Zheng. When Deguang destroyed Jin he summoned him, accused him of betraying his father, and had his flesh eaten—then made Chengxin governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖贈光遠尚書令，封齊王，命中書舍人張正撰光遠碑銘文賜承信，使刻石於青州。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu posthumously appointed Guangyuan Grand Secretary and enfeoffed him Prince of Qi, ordered Secretariat drafter Zhang Zheng to compose his stele inscription and give it to Chengxin to carve in stone at Qing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu posthumously made him Grand Secretary and Prince of Qi and ordered Zhang Zheng to write his epitaph for carving at Qing.

sentences.zh: 碑石既立，天大雷電，擊折之。

translations.literal: When the stele stone was set up, heaven sent great thunder and lightning and struck it broken.
translations.idiomatic: When the stone was raised, thunder shattered it.

sentences.zh: 阿噔啜初非姓氏，其後改名瑊而姓楊氏。

translations.literal: Adengchuo at first was not a surname; later he changed his name to Jian and took the surname Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Adengchuo was not originally a surname; later he took the name Jian and the surname Yang.

sentences.zh: 光遠初名檀，清泰二年，有司言明宗廟諱犯偏傍者皆易之，乃賜名光遠云。

translations.literal: Guangyuan's original name was Tan; in the second year of Qingtai the authorities said those violating Mingzong's temple taboo by partial resemblance should all change—he was then granted the name Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Tan. In Qingtai 2 taboo rules forced a change to Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 光遠既病禿，而妻又跛其足也，人為之語曰：「自古豈有禿瘡天子、跛腳皇后邪？

translations.literal: Guangyuan was afflicted with baldness and his wife too was lame in the foot; people made a saying of it: "Since antiquity has there ever been a bald, scabby Son of Heaven and a lame-footed empress!
translations.idiomatic: Bald himself, with a lame wife, people joked: "Was there ever a scabby emperor and a limping empress?

sentences.zh: 」相傳以為笑。

translations.literal: The tale passed around as laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The joke spread.

sentences.zh: 然而召夷狄為天下首禍，卒滅晉氏，瘡痍中國者三十餘年，皆光遠為之也。

translations.literal: Yet it was he who summoned the barbarians as the realm's chief calamity, at last destroyed the Jin house, and wounded China for more than thirty years—all was done by Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it was he who called the barbarians as the realm's chief scourge, destroyed Jin, and ravaged China for thirty years.
